a: A GraphQL query reads data and lets the client specify exact fields.
Mutations change data (create/update/delete) on the server.
Subscriptions stream real-time updates over WebSocket or similar.
The schema defines types, queries, mutations, and relationships.
Resolvers are functions that fetch the data for each field.
GraphQL can cause N+1 fetches; DataLoader batches and caches per request.
Introspection lets clients discover the schema; disable or restrict in production if needed.
Variables pass dynamic values into queries without string concatenation.
Fragments reuse field selections across multiple queries.
Federation composes multiple GraphQL services into one graph.
Use GraphQL for flexible client-driven reads; REST is simpler for uniform public resources.
Apollo Client is a popular GraphQL client with cache and hooks.
